referent_summary: Amodei's prediction about AI eliminating entry-level white-collar jobs and raising unemployment
source_of_truth: Dario Amodei (CEO, Anthropic), Axios 'Behind the Curtain' interview
authoritative_statement: Amodei said AI could eliminate up to half of entry-level white-collar jobs and push unemployment to 10-20% within one to five years.
epistemic_basis: No study or model published alongside; rests on fast capability growth + rapid deployment + no offsetting job creation.
notes: SOURCE: Primary: Axios 'Behind the Curtain' by VandeHei & Allen, 2025-05-28.

referent_summary: Goldman Sachs estimate of global job-task exposure to generative AI
source_of_truth: Goldman Sachs Research (Briggs & Kodnani), 'The Potentially Large Effects of AI on Economic Growth'
authoritative_statement: Report estimated generative AI is exposed to work equivalent to ~300 million full-time jobs globally and could affect up to two-thirds of US/EU occupations to some degree.
epistemic_basis: Exposure = share of tasks automatable or augmentable, not jobs lost; same report projects productivity/GDP gains.
notes: SOURCE: Primary: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research, 2023-03-26.

referent_summary: IMF estimate of the share of jobs exposed to AI
source_of_truth: IMF (Georgieva / staff discussion note), 'Gen-AI: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Work'
authoritative_statement: IMF estimated ~40% of jobs worldwide are exposed to AI, rising to ~60% in advanced economies, with roughly half of exposed jobs potentially benefiting and half potentially harmed.
epistemic_basis: Occupation -> estimated task exposure -> share of employment; 'exposure' is explicitly bidirectional (help or harm), not 'at risk'.
notes: Frequent distortion target: 'exposed' misread as 'at risk / will be lost'. | SOURCE: Primary: IMF Staff Discussion Note SDN/2024/001, 2024-01-14.

referent_summary: WEF Future of Jobs projections of gross job displacement and creation
source_of_truth: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Reports 2023 and 2025
authoritative_statement: The 2025 report projected 92 million jobs displaced and 170 million created by 2030 (net positive), with large gross churn.
epistemic_basis: Based on surveyed employer expectations; net effect framed positive; survey sentiment is a weak predictor of outcomes.
notes: SOURCE: Primary: WEF report page; press release 2025-01-08.

referent_summary: Zuckerberg's claim that AI will match a mid-level engineer

referent_summary: Huang's claim that AI removes the need to learn to code
source_of_truth: Jensen Huang (CEO, NVIDIA), World Government Summit, Dubai
authoritative_statement: Huang said AI reduces the need to learn to code because the system effectively becomes the programmer, and that everybody is now a programmer.
epistemic_basis: Assertion about skill relevance; contested by educators who argue coding literacy still matters.

referent_summary: McKinsey estimate of generative AI value and automation of work activities
source_of_truth: McKinsey Global Institute, 'The economic potential of generative AI'
authoritative_statement: MGI estimated generative AI could add trillions in value and that half of today's work activities could be automated between roughly 2030 and 2060.
epistemic_basis: Automation timelines span decades with wide uncertainty; framed largely as augmentation.
notes: SOURCE: Primary: McKinsey Digital, 2023-06-14.

referent_summary: Acemoglu's modest estimate of AI task automation and productivity effect
source_of_truth: Daron Acemoglu (MIT), 'The Simple Macroeconomics of AI'
authoritative_statement: Acemoglu estimated AI will automate on the order of 5% of tasks over ~10 years, with small productivity and GDP gains.
epistemic_basis: A macro model with stated assumptions; disputes optimistic capability/compounding assumptions.
notes: SOURCE: Primary: NBER WP 32487, 2024; pub. Economic Policy 40(121):13-58, 2025.

referent_summary: Autor's argument that AI could help rebuild middle-class work
source_of_truth: David Autor (MIT), Noema Magazine essay 'How AI Could Help Rebuild the Middle Class'
authoritative_statement: Autor argued AI could help rebuild middle-skill, middle-class work by extending expertise to more workers, contingent on deployment and policy choices.
epistemic_basis: Honestly scoped: framed as a conditional possibility, not a prediction. Load-bearing assumption (the enabling choices) is not asserted to occur.
notes: Candidate for subclaim decomposition ONLY if his stated mechanisms are pulled from the source; none invented here. | SOURCE: Primary: NBER WP 32140 (drafted for the Noema essay 'How AI Could Help Rebuild the Middle Class'), Feb 2024.

referent_summary: Stanford finding of employment declines among young workers in AI-exposed jobs
source_of_truth: Brynjolfsson, Chandar & Chen (Stanford Digital Economy Lab), 'Canaries in the Coal Mine?'
authoritative_statement: Study found employment declines for workers aged 22-25 in the most AI-exposed occupations, while older workers in the same fields held up.
epistemic_basis: Correlational and early; authors caution other factors (rates, post-pandemic normalization) may contribute.
notes: Preprint. | SOURCE: Primary: Stanford Digital Economy Lab; first circulated Aug 2025, rev. Nov 2025.

referent_summary: Humlum & Vestergaard finding of minimal early labor-market effect from AI chatbots
source_of_truth: Anders Humlum & Emilie Vestergaard, study of AI chatbot adoption (Denmark)
authoritative_statement: Study found generative AI's measured effect on jobs and wages was minimal across occupations studied.
epistemic_basis: Early window; may not capture later, more capable models.
notes: Preprint. | SOURCE: Primary: NBER WP 33777 (also BFI/SSRN), 'Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects,' 2025. Precise null effects, ruling out effects larger than ~1-2%.

referent_summary: Sanders' claims about AI job losses and a shorter work week

authoritative_statement: Sanders argued AI-related displacement could drive large white-collar losses and called for responses including a shorter (32-hour) work week.
epistemic_basis: Advocacy framing; displacement scale asserted, not yet evidenced in aggregate data.

referent_summary: SAG-AFTRA / WGA claims that studio AI use threatens actors' and writers' work
source_of_truth: SAG-AFTRA and WGA, 2023 Hollywood strikes and resulting contract provisions
authoritative_statement: The unions argued studio use of AI threatens members' livelihoods and likenesses, requiring consent and compensation protections; contracts added AI guardrails.
epistemic_basis: Position advanced in bargaining; studios argued some AI uses are complementary.
notes: SOURCE: Primary: official SAG-AFTRA 2023 TV/Theatrical AI resources page (contract ratified 2023-12-05). WGA 2023 MBA has separate AI provisions.

referent_summary: MIT NANDA finding that most enterprise GenAI pilots show no P&L impact
source_of_truth: MIT NANDA initiative, 'The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025'

referent_summary: Finding that LLMs show covert dialect prejudice against African American English

referent_summary: US data-center electricity consumption figures (level and trajectory)

referent_summary: Estimates of energy per typical AI text query
